available_outcomes.name: Mortality
available_outcomes.source_quote:
Table 3. Fluid Requirements and Other Outcomes | Mortality | No TXA (n = 150) 23% | TXA (n = 150) 31% | p = 0.091. 
[Note: Event counts derived from percentages and stated total deaths: 150 * 0.31 = 46.5; 150 * 0.23 = 34.5. Total deaths = 81. 46 + 35 = 81.]

available_outcomes.name: Mortality (excluding DOA)
available_outcomes.source_quote:
Table 3. Fluid Requirements and Other Outcomes | Mortality (excluding DOA) | No TXA 17% | TXA 27% | p = 0.024. 
...of the 81 deaths, 20 patients arrived in extremis and survived less than 2 hours, despite lifesaving interventions. Those patients were defined as DOA and excluded from both groups. Then, the mortality rate changes and achieves statistical significance with TXA versus no TXA (27% vs. 17%, p = 0.024). 
[Note: Derived N and events algebraically since 20 patients were excluded from the total 300, leaving N=280 and 61 deaths. 134 * 0.27 = 36 deaths; 146 * 0.17 = 25 deaths. 36 + 25 = 61.]

quotes.confounding: TXA was given at the attending surgeon’s discretion, other variables may have determined the need for the TXA.
quotes.selection: Consecutive trauma patients (n = 1,217) who required emergency surgery (OR) and/or transfusions... were reviewed. With the use of propensity scores... these patients were matched...
quotes.classification: TXA was made available in the formulary... Resuscitation flow sheets, OR/anesthesia reports, and intensive care unit (ICU) records were reviewed.
quotes.missingData: Mortality data derived directly from trauma registry data.
quotes.measurement: Dead on arrival (DOA) was defined as a patient who arrived in extremis and who survived less than 2 hours...
quotes.reporting: The paper reports mortality and clinical endpoints fully consistent with methods.
